content_sections.heading: About CSIR-NML
content_sections.text: CSIR-NML is a constituent laboratory of the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR), an autonomous body under the Government of India's Ministry of Science and Technology. According to the notice, it is a research and development organisation dedicated to metallurgy and materials engineering research. It is located at Burmamines, Jamshedpur, Jharkhand-831007. The notice states that CSIR-NML aims for a workforce that reflects gender balance and encourages women candidates to apply.

content_sections.heading: Vacancy Details
content_sections.text: The notice lists 28 vacancies across 12 post codes. The number of vacancies against each post code is tentative and may increase or decrease. Pay Level-2 applies to all of them. Of the 28 posts, 3 are reserved for ex-servicemen. One post under T-04 is reserved for PwBD with locomotor disability [OA, OL, BL], which includes Dwarfism (Dw) and Acid Attack Victims (AAV). One post under T-08 is reserved for PwBD in the B (blind)/LV (low vision) category. Of the 7 posts under T-04, 2 are reserved for the Digha centre and 2 for the NML Madras centre.

content_sections.heading: Who Can Apply
content_sections.text: Applicants must be citizens of India. The qualification pattern is the same for every post code, with the trade changing. A candidate needs 10th/Secondary or equivalent examination with minimum 55% marks with science subjects, together with one of the following in the trade of the post code applied for: ITI certificate or National/State Trade Certificate in the trade; OR 2 years' full-time experience as an apprentice in the trade from a recognised institute; OR 3 years' work experience in the trade in a Ministry/Department/Organisation/Public Sector Undertaking/Autonomous Body under the Government of India/State/UT. The prescribed qualifications and experience are minimum. Holding a higher qualification does not replace them. Upper age limit, qualification, experience and validity of certificates are all counted as on the last date of receipt of online applications. Candidates claiming a qualification as equivalent must submit the order or letter, with its number and date, under which it is treated as equivalent. Candidates should check the official notification for the details of each post code.

content_sections.heading: Pay and Tenure
content_sections.text: The posts are at Pay Level-2 (Rs. 19,900-63,200). The notice puts total emoluments at about Rs. 37,000 per month, including house rent allowance and transport allowance at the minimum pay scale applicable in Jamshedpur. Dearness Allowance, House Rent Allowance and Transport Allowance are paid as admissible to central government employees and applicable to CSIR. Council employees are eligible for accommodation under the CSIR Residence Allotment Rules-2022, subject to availability. In that case HRA is not payable. If the Director, CSIR-NML makes it compulsory, selected candidates must stay in CSIR-NML staff quarters. Medical reimbursement, leave travel concession, computer advance and house building advance are available as per CSIR rules. All new recruits come under the New Pension Scheme (contributory), as adopted by CSIR for employees joining on or after 01.01.2004. Selected candidates are on probation for two years from joining; the competent authority may extend or reduce this. Appointment is governed by the Central Civil Services (Conduct) Rules, 1964 and the Central Civil Services (Classification, Control and Appeal) Rules, 1965, as amended from time to time.

content_sections.heading: Place of Posting
content_sections.text: The general place of appointment is CSIR-NML, Jamshedpur. Appointees may also be posted to the CSIR-NML units at Digha (West Bengal) and Chennai, and, at the discretion of the competent authority, to any section or division of CSIR-NML or any CSIR laboratory or institute in India, including its regional centres. Selected candidates may be placed in any division or section of CSIR-NML according to the trade.

content_sections.heading: How to Apply for CSIR-NML Recruitment 2026
content_sections.text: Apply online only through the CSIR-NML website https://nml.res.in . The notice gives the application portal address as https://tiru.ngri.res.in/nml_tech/ . No other mode of application is accepted. Submit the application between 15.12.2026 (10:00 AM) and 08.01.2027 (5:00 PM). The notice advises applicants not to wait for the last date or time. Submit one application for a post code. To apply for more than one post code, submit a separate application and pay a separate fee for each. Registration is needed only once. Two or more applications for one post code may lead to cancellation of candidature. Keep a valid, active personal email ID until the recruitment process is complete and enter it in the form. Create a new one first if you do not have one. Upload a recent (not older than three months) colour passport-size photograph taken without cap or glasses with both ears visible (up to 50 KB). Upload the full signature in black ink on plain white paper (up to 30 KB); it must not be in capital letters. Pay the Rs. 500 fee through the SBI Collect link given in the online form. Select Any Category as the category, then the application fee type, and Regular Appointment as the type of application. Keep the payment receipt. Scan the documents listed below and upload them as PDF files of up to 3 MB each. If your university or board awards CGPA/SGPA/OGPA grades, convert them to percentage by its formula and enter it in the form. Keep the computer-generated application. No hard copy of the application or its attachments is to be sent. A submitted application cannot be withdrawn. For technical problems while filling the form, the notice gives the helpline email [email protected] and phone 0657-2345158. CSIR-NML is not responsible if an application or fee payment is not completed for any reason.

content_sections.heading: Selection and Interview
content_sections.text: Selection has three stages: shortlisting by the screening committee, a trade test (qualifying test) and a competitive written examination. The notice does not describe an interview stage. Candidates recommended by the screening committee are invited for the trade test in the concerned trade/subject. The committee adopts its own criteria to shortlist candidates; having the prescribed minimum qualification and experience alone does not entitle a candidate to be called. Applicants should therefore mention all relevant qualifications and experience in the application, with supporting documents. Candidates who pass the trade test are invited for the written examination. It is an OMR-based or computer-based objective multiple-choice test of 150 questions in 2 hours 30 minutes, at SSC + ITI / Class 12 level. Questions are in English and Hindi, except the English language questions. Paper I has no negative marking. Papers II and III carry one negative mark for each wrong answer. The Mental Ability Test covers general intelligence, quantitative aptitude, reasoning ability, problem solving and situational judgement. Papers II and III are evaluated only for candidates who score the minimum marks in Paper I, which the selection committee will decide. The final merit list is based on marks in Papers II and III. For equal marks, merit is decided in the following order, as per the CSIR circular dated 30.05.2023: Higher marks in the papers of the relevant subject/trade. Lower negative marks in the papers of the relevant subject/trade, where applicable. Lower negative marks in the papers considered for merit, where applicable. Older candidate by date of birth. Candidate who acquired the essential educational qualification earlier. Alphabetical order of the candidates' first names. Candidates with benchmark disabilities who are allowed a scribe or reader get 20 extra minutes per hour of the examination. Candidates entitled to a scribe who do not use one also get the 20 extra minutes. Candidates must email [email protected] at least 15 days before the examination to request a scribe/reader. A candidate may choose their own scribe or use the one arranged by CSIR-NML. A personal scribe must be one qualification level below the candidate's and cannot be a candidate in the same examination.
